text: Hello, and welcome to live coverage of this fixture in the Premier League, as West Ham United host title-chasing Arsenal in a London derby at the Olympic Stadium.
The Irons are yet to win a match across any competition so far in 2024, and suffered a 3-0 defeat to Manchester United in their last Premier League game following three successive draws.

Their last league victory did come in the reverse fixture at the Emirates though, beating Arsenal 2-0 on December 28th, and despite their poor run of form, West Ham will climb to sixth should they claim all three points at the London Stadium.

Arsenal, on the other hand, have won all three of their league fixtures so far this calendar year, responding from a 2-0 FA Cup loss to Liverpool by thumping Crystal Palace and edging Nottingham Forest respectively.

The Gunners returned the favour against Liverpool too, defeating the league leaders 3-1 at home last time out, and another win here will take Mikel Arteta’s side back to within two points of the Premier League summit.
David Moyes names an unchanged starting XI in the Premier League for the first time since October, when they played the same XI in five consecutive matches.

James Ward-Prowse has netted penalties in two of West Ham’s last three games, and plays in behind striker Jarrod Bowen, while Tomas Soucek, who scored the opener at the Emirates in late December, is in a double-pivot alongside Edson Alvarez.
Mikel Arteta makes two changes for the Gunners, bringing Jakub Kiwior and Leandro Trossard into the XI.

Kiwior is a like-for-like replacement for Oleksandr Zinchenko at left-back, while Trossard will lead the line up front, flanked by Bukayo Saka and Gabriel Martinelli and pushing Kai Havertz back into midfield.
The teams head out onto the London Stadium pitch amidst a sea of West Ham bubbles, and we'll be underway in just a matter of moments here!
Trossard will get the game underway, and kicks off another London derby at the Olympic Stadium in Stratford!
Kudus dispossesses Kiwior and bursts forward threatening to open Arsenal up.
He turns and frees Coufal up for a cross, but his ball into the box is headed away by Gabriel at the near post.
Odegaard advances to the edge of West Ham's box and looks to link up with Trossard, but the Belgian takes a poor touch and it rolls on through to Areola.
Bowen makes a run in behind the defence and gets a shot away to test Areola, but everyone else in the stadium has seen the correctly raised offside flag to give Arsenal a free-kick.
West Ham are looking to complete a Premier League double over Arsenal for the first time since 2006-07, following their 2-0 win at the Emirates in December.
They also defeated the Gunners 3-1 in a home EFL Cup tie in November.
Odegaard looks to float a ball into the box from deep with Trossard making the run, but Zouma gets there ahead of the forward and heads clear for West Ham.
Martinelli is found in space with a cross-field pass to the left.
He whips the ball back in towards the six-yard box, but Aguerd's flick takes the ball behind for a corner.

Areola's throw out from the collected corner is too long for Alvarez, but the Mexican chases on and slides in recklessly on Saka! He's shown a yellow card by the referee for that mistimed challenge, and Gabriel's not happy with Alvarez either.
Rice's first-time ball into the middle is met by Havertz from close-range, but there's no direction on his looping header and Areola collects easily enough.
BLOCKED!!! Saka has Arsenal's first real sight of goal with a speculative shot from 25 yards, which bounces up and takes a deflection off Aguerd to go behind for a corner!
Odegaard's cross to the far post is attacked by the arriving Kiwior, but Alvarez gets goal-side of the defender and glances it behind for another Arsenal set-piece.
Arsenal have won nine and lost just one of their last 15 Premier League away games against West Ham, going down 1-0 in January 2019.
Current Gunner Declan Rice scored the winner for the Hammers that day.
CHANCE!!! Johnson and Bowen combine to play a superb one-two down the left-hand side.
Johnson drills a low cross in towards Kudus arriving in the centre, but Kiwior does just enough to get a touch on the ball and send it behind for a corner!
West Ham already have beaten Arsenal twice in the Premier League and EFL Cup so far this season.
The last London side to beat the Gunners three times in the same campaign were Chelsea in 2005-06, with West Ham only doing so once - back in 1924-25.
BLOCKED!! Martinelli's loose pass is snatched onto by Bowen, who turns and charges at the backtracking Arsenal defence.
He lines up a shot from distance and lets fly, but a block from Gabriel sends the ball looping into Raya's gloves!
Saka rides the attempted challenge of Alvarez and shrugs off Emerson to get a shot away from the edge of the box, but his final effort is a poor one and rolls meekly goalwards for Areola to collect.
OVER!!! Saka cuts inside and fizzes a cross in to Trossard, who rises in the middle but can't keep his glancing header on target as it flashes over the bar!
WHAT A SAVE THAT IS!! Martinelli shifts to the right and is put in behind by Saka's throughball.
He scoops a cross back for Trossard to hit goalwards, and the Belgian meets it with a powerful first-time volley that is somehow tipped over the bar thanks to miraculous reflexes by Areola!
Saka's initial delivery is punched clear before being recovered by Martinelli, whose cross back into the middle is met by Trossard glancing another headed effort wide!

This is the 11th time that Leandro Trossard, Gabriel Martinelli and Bukayo Saka have started a Premier League match together, with Arsenal winning eight of the previous 10 and averaging 2.3 goals per game in the process.
BLOCKED!!! Odegaard's snap-shot from the edge of the box is driven low, taking a deflection off Emerson which wrong-foots Areola and takes the ball behind for another Arsenal corner!
Rice's drilled throughball puts Martinelli scampering in behind the defence, and he sends a pacy, low cross into the middle.
Both Odegaard and Saka are chasing it, but Aguerd gets a foot in to clear the ball before either can capitalise!
Just the 69 per cent possession, nine shots and three on target so far for Arsenal, who are dominating this contest in almost every single area - aside from the scoreline of course.

GOOOOOOOAAAAAALLLL!!!!! Arsenal make a deserved breakthrough!!! Rice swings the corner into a crowded West Ham box, and Saliba climbs above the rest at the far post to nod a simple header in from close range!! You can't say it hasn't been coming, and the Gunners lead 1-0 to make their dominance count!
An on-the-money delivery from Rice, leaving West Ham's defence and goalkeeper stranded as Saliba rose to get on the end of it.
That's Saliba's second goal of the season, and the 11th Arsenal have scored from corners so far this campaign, the most of any side in the Premier League.
WIDE!!! Kiwior stands up a cross for Saka at the far post, but the England forward gets the direction on his effort all wrong, heading across the face of goal and wide of the upright!
CHANCE!!! Wide once more from Saka!!! He's put through on goal by Odegaard's threaded pass between three defenders, and engages the onrushing Areola.
He dinks the ball goalwards with the keeper stranded, but it rolls slowly wide of the same post!
PENALTY TO ARSENAL!!! The Gunners have a golden chance to go 2-0 up here!! Saka times his run to perfection to get on the end of Trossard's lofted pass over the top, and knocks the ball past Areola.
The West Ham goalkeeper can't get out of the way and takes Saka to ground, giving the referee no choice but to point to the spot!
Areola's shown a yellow card for that foul, with only the presence of Aguerd in the box preventing the colour of that card from being red.
There's a quick VAR check to see if Saka was definitely onside from his initial run, but it's cleared by the officials and Saka will step up from 12 yards!
GOOOOOAAAAALLL!!! Saka doubles Arsenal's lead!!! An excellent penalty, swept with power into the bottom-right corner and sending Areola the wrong way.
Arsenal have hit another gear since going a goal up, and now lead 2-0 following an expert spot-kick from Saka!
Saka has now contributed to five goals in his last five Premier League games with four strikes and one assist, and that penalty brings him to nine for the season.
GOOOOAAAAALLL!!!! The Gunners are running away with this one!!! They win a free-kick on the left touchline which is arrowed into the box by Rice.

Both Havertz and Gabriel attack it at the front post, and it's the Brazilian who gets the final touch to head beyond Areola at the near post!!! 3-0 to the visitors, who are running riot at the London Stadium!
A second assist of the half for Rice against his former club, and for all the West Ham fans won't be happy with him for that, their defending has been shambolic since Saliba opened the scoring.
Another SEVEN minutes of added time to play at the London Stadium, and Arsenal might must fancy their chances of grabbing another goal before half-time does come.
GOOOOOOAAAALLL!!!!! There's number four for Arsenal - how good is this from the Gunners!! They cut through West Ham with ease once more as Odegaard dribbles forward and finds Trossard in the box.
He cuts onto his right foot and curls a beautiful shot towards goal, which Areola gets a hand to but can't keep out of the top corner!!! 4-0 now, and how many can Arsenal get at this rate?
A simple ball forward from Odegaard yields another Arsenal goal, forcing the West Ham defence to stand off and giving Trossard the space to curl their fourth home.
Rice has provided two assists in a Premier League match for the very first time in his 228th match, while Odegaard's is his third in seven appearances against West Ham.

The West Ham fans are leaving in droves - and that's putting it lightly - well before the half-time whistle, and it's hardly surprising given how their side have fallen to pieces in the last few minutes.
They were defending pretty well for the first half-hour or so!
HALF-TIME: WEST HAM 0-4 ARSENAL.
Well, how best to describe that first half? Arsenal head into the break an astonishing 4-0 up following a dominant performance in every sense of the word.
Early chances for Saka, Trossard and Odegaard were all blocked or saved as West Ham kept their shape in defence, but that shape fell to pieces following Saliba's opening goal from a far-post header.
A defence-splitting run from Saka soon yielded a penalty for Arsenal, and the forward made it 2-0 from the spot.
The one-way traffic continued at pace, with Gabriel heading in another Rice cross just three minutes later, and the Irons' misery was compounded by Trossard curling in number four in stoppage time.

The London Stadium is emptying at a rapid rate with many West Ham fans having seen more than enough in that first half, and you get the sense that the second period will be a case of damage limitation for the hosts.
Saka has lead from the front in Arsenal's scorching attacking display thus far, having six attempts on goal and burying his only one on target into the bottom corner from 12 yards.

events.action: burying his only one on target into the bottom corner

text: His seven touches in the box and 1.38 xG have been supported by 22 final-third passes - two of which have created big chances - as well as winning six of 10 duels, two dribbles and aerial contests apiece.
Saka has also recovered possession four times for the Gunners, twice doing so in the final third as well as winning two free-kicks.
Revelation.
West Ham make a pair of half-time changes in a bid to turn their luck around in the second period, with the booked Alvarez replaced by Kalvin Phillips in the centre of midfield.
Former Arsenal defender Konstantinos Mavropanos scored the Hammers' second in their 2-0 win five league games ago, but comes on Zouma in entirely different circumstances this time around.
Bowen kicks the second half off for West Ham, who have one hell of a mountain to climb if they're to spark any sort of comeback in the next 45 minutes.
Martinelli beats Coufal around the outside and cuts the ball back for Trossard, but he fluffs his lines with a first-time finish that is sent looping high and wide of the target!

Arsenal are unbeaten in their last 34 Premier League matches when leading at half-time and have won all seven such games this term, with that run dating back to January 2022's 2-1 loss against Manchester City.
WIDE!!! Havertz sizes up a shot from 20-yard and finds space to strike goalwards, but his low drive rolls just wide of Areola's left-hand post with the goalkeeper at full stretch!
Kudus and Johnson both try their luck from the edge of the Arsenal box, but Rice and Gabriel get in front of each respective shot to keep the Hammers at bay.
Today is only the second time that West Ham have conceded four times in the first half of a Premier League home match.
The other was against Leeds United back in November 2002, when they were 4-1 down at half-time and went on to lose 4-3.
Trossard and Saka try a one-two on the edge of West Ham's box, but Emerson slides in with perfect timing to hook the ball away from the latter's feet.

SAVED!!! Odegaard and Havertz combine in the box and link up with Saka, who waltzes through two challenges and fires a shot goalwards which Areola sticks out a big right hand to parry away from danger!
West Ham had only conceded three first-half goals across all their Premier League home games combined this season, making the four they've let Arsenal score in this match look all the more freakish!

The second half has continued in much the same vein as the first ended for both sides, with West Ham chasing shadows and Arsenal strolling through meek defence wherever possible - waiting for their moment to add another goal.
GOOOOAAAAALLLL!!!! A five-star performance yields goal number five for Arsenal!!! Odegaard finds Saka, who turns on the edge of the box and looks to shoot towards the far corner.

Areola guesses that way too, but Saka leaves the goalkeeper helpless as he drills a low shot into the bottom-right corner for 5-0!!! The Gunners are back up and running in the second half, as the onslaught continues in east London.
Odegaard gets another assist, his second of the match, with a simple ball forward which Saka turned to gold.

GOOOOOAAAAALLL!!!! Number six for Arsenal, and that one will really sting for the West Ham faithful!! White arrives in the box to get on the end of Martinelli's dinked ball, and passes back to the edge of the area.

Trossard and Odegaard both leave it, but Rice doesn't, smashing a first-time thunderbolt which fizzes beyond Areola and into the top-left corner!! A sensational finish not matched by the former Hammer's muted celebration, who adds insult to injury by making it 6-0.
White's ball was simply asking to be hit goalwards, and after Trossard and Odegaard declined the offer, Rice stepped up to take it with both hands.
That ridiculous Rice finish will be his last action of the contest, coming off for Mohamed Elneny with the points firmly in the bag.
Eddie Nketiah also comes on in Arsenal's second change, and he replaces another goalscorer in Trossard up front.
Saka's brace has been one of many highlights in this enigmatic Gunners performance, but he won't get the chance of a hat-trick as Reiss Nelson comes on to complete the triple change.
Declan Rice comes off having been involved in three goals (one goal, two assists) in a Premier League match for the very first time in his career.
West Ham think they've won a corner after Gabriel blocks Ward-Prowse's low cross behind, but an earlier foul on his namesake Martinelli results in a free-kick to the Gunners instead.
SAVED!!!! Nelson slips in the box and can't get on the end of Odegaard's cutback from the byline, but Elneny comes onto the ball at pace and hits a decent first-time effort into the gloves of Areola!
SAVED!!! Havertz advances down the left and links up with Nketiah just inside the box, but the substitute's right-footed effort towards the far corner is saved and held by Areola!
Kudus competes for the ball with Martinelli before losing out to the Arsenal wideman, clipping him late and earning the Ghanaian a yellow card for thus troubles.
West Ham make another change as Aaron Cresswell comes on, replacing a limping Emerson at left-back for the final 15 minutes or so.
Two more changes are also on the way for Arsenal, as the Premier League's youngest-ever player Ethan Nwaneri, 15 at the time of his debut in 2022, enters proceedings in place of Martinelli.
White also comes off at right-back as Mikel Arteta's side round off their changes, with Cedric Soares on in his place.
Arsenal captain Odegaard has now created 12 chances in his two Premier League appearances against West Ham this season, with six in December's 2-0 loss and five more (and counting) this time around.
Nelson and Nwaneri both find themselves crowded out in the box and the latter tees up Elneny on the edge, whose side-footed effort sails well wide of the intended target.
BLOCKED!!! Kudus dribbles in behind Elneny and tries to cut the ball back before Raya gets a foot in, and Gabriel does likewise to deny Bowen from the follow-up as West Ham win a rare corner!
Ward-Prowse looks to put one of his specialist set-piece deliveries into the box, but sends the out-swinger straight into the waiting gloves of Raya.
Nelson tries to clip the ball into Nketiah's path in the centre, but his cross takes a deflection and the striker can't get on the end of it!
This is on course to be West Ham's heaviest ever home defeat in the Premier League.
All four previous occasions that the Hammers have lost by a six-goal margin have been on the road.

Nelson whips an Arsenal free-kick into the area from a similar position to which Rice crossed for Gabriel in the first half, but the Brazilian can't connect properly with this one and West Ham come away with possession.
We're set for three added minutes at the London Stadium, which West Ham players, coaches and fans alike will be over as quickly as possible.
Phillips slides in wildly on Nelson as the winger collects a pass from Nketiah, as the West Ham midfielder gets none of the ball but does receive a late yellow card for the challenge.
FULL-TIME: WEST HAM 0-6 ARSENAL.
Arsenal add another two second-half goals to their four-goal buffer from the first 45 minutes, completing a resounding and record-breaking 6-0 victory at the London Stadium.
Any hope of West Ham responding after half-time was soon quashed by Bukayo Saka, who lashed in his second and Arsenal's fifth goal in the 63rd minute.

Further salt was rubbed in West Ham wounds two minutes later, as former captain Declan Rice thumped in a piledriving effort from 25 yards to make it 6-0, with no signs of life coming from the home side.

Substitutes Elneny and Nketiah both drew late saves from Areola as Arsenal refused to lower the ante, but no further goals would come as the Gunners go level on points - and goal difference - with second-placed Manchester City.
Their biggest ever home defeat in the Premier League leaves West Ham eighth in the table, and that 6-0 drubbing is a result they need to bounce back from as quickly as possible.
